name: Pennyweight

stars.name: Pennyweight
stars.notes: Old, even-tempered dwarf whose slow burn promises billions of years of stable trade seasons.

planets.name: Cinderclip
planets.notes: Cracked airless rock worked for rare iridium veins by teleoperated cutters.

planets.name: Weighstone
planets.notes: Habitability-zone world turning so slowly that its terminator villages live in permanent golden hour; the tiered orchards are famous across four sectors.

planets.name: Dunmark
planets.notes: Gray way-marker world used for navigation drills and nothing else.

planets.name: Ballast
planets.notes: Hydrogen-scooping stop for departing freighter convoys.

planets.name: Sleetscale
planets.notes: Comet-nursery moonlet field at the system's cold edge.

asteroid_belts.name: Clipstone Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: League-licensed smelter hulks chain-mine the nickel-iron body; unlicensed cutting draws fast, expensive fines.

stations.name: The Minting Yard
stations.notes: Seat of the Weightmasters' League; master cargo weights are certified nowhere else in the Span.

stations.name: Clippings Terminal
stations.notes: Ore transfer and crew rotation hub for the smelter fleet.

stations.name: Orange Watch
stations.notes: League patrol base guarding the convoy lanes through the junction.

stations.name: Farthing Deep
stations.notes: Last bunkerage before the long haul out; fuel, repair, and rumor.

faction_control.notes: A merchant league in all but name: certified weighmasters set policy, defense is contracted out, and every berth fee is published openly.

history: Founded as a certification depot where cargo scales from forty systems could be checked against one master standard.
The League Charter was signed aboard the Minting Yard after the Scale Wars left smaller ports desperate for neutral ground.
Recent convoy surges have pushed berth queues past ninety days, prompting quiet talk of a second yard.
description: An amber lamp of a star, Pennyweight holds five close-knit orbits in its long, even warmth. Weighstone turns so slowly that its terminator villages never leave the golden hour, and its stair-step orchards are visible from high dock. Beyond gray Dunmark, the metallic glitter of the Clipstone Belt divides the inner trades from the gas fields.

As the only major junction threading the Span, the system funnels convoys from dozens of routes through one certified corridor. The Weightmasters' League keeps order with published tariffs rather than warships, though Orange Watch sees plenty of drill time. Nearly two million people live and work somewhere in the queue.

Berth speculation has become the local obsession, and more than one factor has vanished over futures that never matured. The master standards sealed in the Minting Yard have drifted four grams since founding—or so an expelled apprentice claims. Nobody in authority will re-measure them.
